readerTitle: Why Avon's best salesperson was the neighbor
caseNote: 실제 기업 (Avon: 창업, 방문판매 모델, 백화점 전용 라인 시도) + 창업 일화 + 가상 적용 (산업용 부품 제조사)
insight: 방문판매원이 판 것은 화장품이 아니라 이미 쌓아 둔 신뢰였다. 영업에서는 고객과의 관계를 누가 갖고 있는지가 곧 판매 채널이다.
misconception: 판매 채널은 많을수록 좋다. 같은 제품을 매장에도 놓으면 판매원 매출에 더해 추가 매출이 생긴다.

sources.text: Avon company history pages (founding in 1886 by David H. McConnell, California Perfume Company, first representative Persis Foster Eames Albee, renamed Avon in 1939)

Katina L. Manko, Ding Dong! Avon Calling!: The Women and Men of Avon Products, Incorporated (Oxford University Press, 2021). History of the representative model, the 1950s ad campaign and workplace selling
Avon Products, Inc. records, Hagley Museum and Library (company archive)
Business press coverage (e.g., The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal) of Avon's beComing line at J.C. Penney, about 2001–2004
Natura &Co announcement completing the acquisition of Avon Products, Inc. (January 2020)

factChecks.note: 창업 일화(책 방문판매 중 향수 샘플을 나눠 줬더니 고객이 향수를 더 원했다)는 Avon이 직접 소개하는 이야기이며 다소 미화됐을 수 있습니다. 카드에 "as the company tells it"로 일화임을 밝혔습니다.
1886년 창업, California Perfume Company 이름, 첫 판매원 Persis Foster Eames Albee(뉴햄프셔), 1939년 Avon으로 사명 변경을 Avon 공식 역사 자료로 확인하세요.
"Ding dong, Avon calling" 광고는 1950년대(보통 1954년 TV 광고로 소개)입니다. 카드에는 "in the 1950s"로만 적었습니다.
beComing 라인: J.C. Penney 매장 출시(2001년경)와 중단(2003~2004년경), 판매 부진과 판매원 반발 보도를 당시 기사로 확인하세요. 카드에는 구체 수치 없이 "around 2001", "within a few years"로 적었습니다.
고객이 낮에 집에 없게 되자 판매원들이 직장(사무실, 휴게실)에서 판매했다는 내용은 Manko(2021) 등 역사 자료로 확인하세요. 정확한 비율은 쓰지 않았습니다.
Natura &Co의 Avon Products 인수 완료는 2020년 1월입니다. 북미 사업은 2016년에 별도 매각되었으므로 카드에는 "most of Avon"이 아니라 "Avon"의 소유권 변화로만 일반적으로 적었습니다. 게시 전 표현을 다시 확인하세요.
2번 카드는 실제 결정 시점을 단순화해 재구성한 것입니다. 선택지 B·C는 Avon이 실제로 한 일(직장 판매 지원, 별도 매장 라인)과 대응하지만, 회사 내부 논의를 그대로 옮긴 것은 아닙니다.

cards.title: Why Avon's best salesperson was the neighbor
body: For more than a century, Avon sold lipstick and perfume without stores. Its products reached customers through local sellers, mostly women selling to people they already knew.
Then customers stopped being home during the day. Avon had to decide what its sellers were really for.

image.label: A neighbor at a front door holding a small product catalog
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 동네 현관 앞에서 이웃 여성이 작은 카탈로그를 들고 웃으며 인사하고, 문 안쪽 사람도 반갑게 맞이함. 따뜻한 오후 햇살. 실제 Avon 로고와 제품 포장은 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Your customers aren't home anymore.
body: It's the late 1990s and you run Avon. Your independent sellers, called representatives, buy at a discount and sell to friends and neighbors. But more of your customers now work outside the home, and department stores sell cosmetics to the same people.

options.text: Put the full product line in department stores
options.feedback: You reach busy shoppers fast. But your sellers now compete with a shelf that carries their own products, and they have less reason to keep selling.

options.text: Help sellers reach customers where they now are, like offices
options.feedback: You keep the relationships that make the model work and follow customers to new places. Growth is slower than a store rollout, but the channel stays intact.

options.text: Launch a separate brand only for stores
options.feedback: Keeping the lines apart softens the clash with sellers. But stores still teach customers they can buy from you without the seller.

cards.title: A free gift that sold better than the books.
body: In the 1880s, David McConnell sold books door to door. As the company tells it, he handed out small perfume samples to get people to listen, and customers wanted the perfume more than the books.

In 1886 he started the California Perfume Company, later renamed Avon. His first seller, Persis Albee of New Hampshire, recruited other women to sell. The pattern held for decades: a local seller, buying at a discount, selling to people who already knew her.

image.label: An old book case with small perfume bottles tucked beside the books
image.brief: 1880년대 느낌의 낡은 가죽 책 가방이 열려 있고, 책 옆에 작은 향수병 샘플들이 꽂혀 있음. 향수병 쪽에 은은한 빛. 실제 상표나 라벨 문구는 넣지 않음.

cards.title: Relationships are a sales channel
body: An Avon representative didn't start with strangers. Her first customers were neighbors, relatives and coworkers. They already trusted her, so she skipped the hardest step in selling: getting someone to listen.

That trust was what Avon really relied on. **The company made the products. The sellers owned the relationships.** Its famous 1950s ads, "Ding dong, Avon calling," sold the friendly visit as much as the lipstick.
cards.softwareNote: Software firms that sell through resellers or consultants depend on the same thing: the partner already has the client's trust. A cheaper direct plan that bypasses partners can win a few deals and lose the channel.

cards.title: The sellers moved. Then Avon tried stores.
body: As customers went to work, many representatives followed them, selling in offices and break rooms. The relationship survived; only the meeting place changed.

Around 2001, Avon also tried retail. It launched a separate line, called beComing, in J.C. Penney department stores. Sales were weak, and many representatives saw the stores as competition. The line was pulled within a few years.

image.label: A seller showing a catalog to coworkers in an office break room
image.brief: 사무실 휴게실에서 한 직원이 동료 두세 명에게 작은 카탈로그를 보여주고 있음. 커피잔, 점심 도시락이 놓인 테이블. 친근한 분위기. 실제 브랜드 로고 없음.

cards.title: A shelf can't copy a person.
body: The store offered the product without the relationship. That created two problems at once.
list: **Customers** who could buy in a store had less reason to order from their seller.
**Sellers** who felt undercut had less reason to push the brand.
cards.callout: The part that made the model work was the part a store couldn't provide.

cards.title: Relationship selling has a ceiling.
body: A seller's circle is finite. Once friends and family have bought, growth depends on recruiting more sellers, and in direct selling many sellers earn little and leave quickly.

Relationships can also wear thin when every coffee turns into a pitch. And trust doesn't fix weak products or prices. Avon kept struggling in later years and changed ownership, joining Brazil's Natura &Co in 2020.

cards.title: Now it's an industrial parts maker.
body: You make bearings and fasteners. Independent distributors sell them, and their reps know every maintenance manager in their region. You're building an online store.

options.text: Sell online at prices below what distributors charge
options.feedback: You may win some price-driven orders. But distributors will push rival brands, and you lose the people who get you into plants.

options.text: Let buyers order online, with each order credited to their local distributor
options.feedback: Customers get convenience and distributors keep their reason to sell you. You give up some margin you might have kept by selling direct.

options.text: Sell direct only to your ten largest accounts
options.feedback: It captures margin where it's biggest. But those are often the accounts distributors worked hardest to win, and they'll notice.

cards.title: Before adding a channel, ask who owns the relationship.
body: Avon's sellers weren't just a delivery route. They were trusted people, and a new channel helps only if it supports them instead of replacing them.

**Try it today:** list your ten best customers. Next to each, write who they trust at your business: a person, a partner or no one. Then ask whether your next channel helps that person or competes with them.
